descriptionChirho: The act of deliberating or taking counsel together (συμβούλιον), especially in a hostile sense of plotting or conspiring, as in the phrase συμβούλιον λαμβάνειν/ποιεῖν ('to take/make counsel') used repeatedly of the chief priests and Pharisees plotting against Jesus (Matthew 12:14, 22:15, 27:1, 27:7, 28:12; Mark 3:6, 15:1). Multilingual evidence: Arabic مَشُورَة (mashūra, 'consultation/counsel'), Korean 의논 (uinon, 'deliberation')/회의 (hoeui, 'meeting'), Swahili shauri ('counsel/plan') and wakashauriana ('they consulted together'), Hindi सलाह (salāh, 'advice')/मशवरा (mashvarā, 'consultation'), Spanish consejo ('counsel'). This is the abstract act of deliberating, not the governing body.

A formal advisory or governing body, a council as an institution (συμβούλιον as concrete noun), appearing in Acts 25:12 where Festus confers with his council (τοῦ συμβουλίου) before responding to Paul's appeal to Caesar. Multilingual evidence distinguishes this from the abstract 'counsel/deliberation' sense: Arabic المَجْلِس (al-majlis, 'the council/assembly'), Korean 자문회 (jamunhoe, 'advisory council'), Swahili baraza ('council/court'), Hindi परिषद (pariṣad, 'council/assembly'), Spanish consejo (here as institutional body). The genitive form and the definite article mark this as a specific established institution, not the act of consulting.
